A pixel-art character portrait for a cosy high-fantasy role-playing game's dialogue box: a chest-up close-up with the face looking straight at the viewer, the head and shoulders square to the camera and centred. Real low-resolution pixel art: the whole picture is a grid of about 96 by 96 big square pixels, each about 10 to 11 image pixels wide, every one a single flat colour, with no anti-aliasing, blur, gradient or texture inside it. A small palette of about 24 to 32 colours in ramps of three or four tones per material: shadows cooler and more violet, highlights warmer and more golden. A one-pixel outline in dark brown-violet, never pure black, around the hair, face and shoulders, with lighter coloured lines inside. Soft, colourful cel shading, lit from above and slightly in front. Normal proportions for a bust (not chibi): the age, people and personality of the character obvious at a glance, and the high-fantasy costume shown at the collar and shoulders as bold, simple shapes (trims, clasps, gems, armour edges, fur). AVOID. Smooth, painterly, vector or high-resolution rendering; small or uneven pixels; gradients; photographic texture or noise; glossy 3D-render shading; pure-black outlines. Sweat drops, anger marks, blush lines or tear streams drawn beside the face (the game adds those). Scenery, a frame, a border, a name plate, a speech bubble.
